title: Zoom at Dreamforce 2026: Connecting intelligence, conversations, and revenue execution
summary: How Zoom's vision for a unified revenue operating system and AI contact center deployment best practices connect buyer signals to pipeline — key takeaways from Dreamforce 2026.
body_markdown:
Dreamforce 2026 was built around one central idea, the Agentic Enterprise, a model where humans and agents drive customer success together.[Zoom CX](https://www.zoom.com/en/audiences/cx/) came with a clear point of view for[CX and revenue leaders](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/customer-experience-resolution-deal-breaker/) : the future of go-to-market is one connected platform.


For CX and revenue leaders, the central lesson from Dreamforce was straightforward: successful AI deployments depend on visibility, actionable workflows, and continuous feedback

## What is a unified revenue operating system?


An intelligent revenue operating system is a connected platform that ties buyer intelligence, customer conversations, and sales execution together, replacing the fragmented stack of disconnected tools that many B2B revenue teams currently rely on. The Agentic Enterprise model Salesforce built Dreamforce 2026 around assumes that agents and humans need to work from the same signals. A revenue operating system is the infrastructure that makes that possible for go-to-market teams.


We position Zoom Revenue Accelerator as the connective layer across four stages of the revenue workflow: identifying in-market buyers, engaging them through coordinated outreach, capturing and learning from every conversation, and converting those signals into actionable pipeline forecasts. The concept matters because the alternative is a familiar one: stitching together tools that don't share a data layer produces insights that arrive too late to act on.


## Two sessions, one story: CX and revenue on the same platform


[Kentis Gopalla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kentisgopalla/) , Head of Product for Zoom CX, took the Dreamforce stage with a session titled "Deployed Isn't Done: Turning AI Investment into Customer Outcomes". The session focused on the gap between launching an AI deployment and delivering measurable customer outcomes.


Kentis presented the Zoom CX product suite, including Contact Center, Virtual Agent, Workforce Management, Quality Management, AI Expert Assist, and CX Insights—as the infrastructure for a five-stage AI maturity loop:


**1. Connected journeys:** Zoom Contact Center and Zoom Virtual Agent work together to create a unified interaction layer. When a customer moves from self-service to a live agent, the context of the conversation travels with them by eliminating the "start over" experience that can erode satisfaction and inflate handle times.


**2. Generated insights:** CX Insights aggregates data across channels and interactions to surface patterns that would otherwise stay buried in individual tickets. Instead of relying on anecdotal escalation reports, CX leaders can get a data-driven view of what customers are actually struggling with and where AI is resolving issues versus where it's falling short.


**3. Routed actions:** AI Expert Assist turns those insights into real-time agent guidance. When a conversation matches a known pattern, Expert Assist can surface knowledge articles, suggested responses, or next steps directly in the agent's workflow so insights don't sit in a dashboard but drive action at the point of interaction.


**4. Measured outcomes:** Quality Management evaluates interactions comprehensively, not just a random sample, against defined criteria. This gives CX leaders a comprehensive picture of how agents and AI are performing, helping to replace the guesswork of spot-check QA with systematic measurement.


**5. Closed-loop learning:** Workforce Management closes the loop by connecting performance data back to coaching and scheduling. When Quality Management identifies a pattern, Workforce Management can route targeted training to relevant agents and inform staffing decisions to match actual demand. Workforce Management uses that performance data to help inform coaching, training, and scheduling adjustments.


Each stage supports a different part of the path from customer interaction to measurable improvement. Skipping measurement or feedback can cause AI investments to plateau after deployment.


"Being able to set guardrails around agents is a key thing, because that's what most of my enterprise customers are asking for," said[Dave Smith](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-smith-6770618/) , Founder and Principal Analyst of Inflow Analysis, after the Workforce Management demonstration.


[Dina Vaccari](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dinavaccari/) , Head of Product for Zoom Revenue Accelerator, addressed the revenue side of the same challenge in "From First Signal to Closed Deal, and Beyond." The session focused on how revenue teams can identify in-market buyers, execute coordinated outreach, learn from conversations, and improve pipeline forecasting, and how the system continuously learns from outcomes, sharpening the next round of outreach, coaching, and forecasting based on what actually happened.


Many B2B sales teams know which accounts are assigned to a territory but do not always know which accounts are actively in-market because they aren't connecting signals to individuals or seeing the research and engagement happening in the dark funnel. Common Room by Zoom shines a light on that activity and helps resolve it to the person level, allowing sellers to map contacts and accounts to actual buying behavior. Zoom's revenue platform is designed to connect those buyer signals, rep conversations, coaching data, and pipeline models so that revenue execution can become more informed and continuously improved, helping to sharpen buyer intelligence across the revenue journey.


Together, the two sessions made a single argument: Zoom CX builds the closed-loop infrastructure that can help turn customer interactions into actionable signals, and Zoom's revenue tools can help turn those signals along with buyer intelligence and conversation data into coordinated pipeline action. The value of either side depends on the other.


## From buyer signals to closed deals


On[September 15, 2026](https://news.zoom.com/zoom-unveils-ai-powered-revenue-os/) , Zoom announced three components designed to connect buyer intelligence, conversations, and revenue execution.


### Common Room by Zoom


[Common Room by Zoom](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/zoom-to-acquire-common-room/) is the buyer intelligence and action foundation of Zoom's revenue operating system. Common Room aggregates signals from product activity, digital engagement, and community interactions to help teams identify in-market accounts, resolved to the person-level view.


These signals give revenue teams a way to prioritize action based on observed buyer behavior rather than relying only on static account lists or manual prospecting. Because Common Room by Zoom is native to the same system as conversation intelligence, engagement and forecasting, signals it surfaces are connected to what happens on calls, in sequences, and in deals, and outcomes write back to sharpen what the system knows.


### Engage


Engage supports multichannel sales sequencing across email, phone, and tasks. Signals surfaced by Common Room's buyer intelligence helps identify in-market accounts before a rep ever makes contact, so sequences inherit real intent rather than a cold list, helping revenue teams move from reactive follow-up to signal driven execution.


Engage helps address the question of when and how to reach out, grounded in real buyer activity, so outreach can be informed and personalized from the start.


### Forecast


Forecast brings together conversation data and customer signals at the company and deal levels. Forecast can suggest updates to CRM systems, helping keep pipeline data current while maintaining rep review within the workflow.


Forecast can help address the question of which deals are most likely to close by grounding pipeline visibility in real conversation and deal intelligence


Together, Engage and Forecast address two major points of friction in B2B sales: knowing who to engage when, and with what messaging, and understanding which opportunities are most likely to convert, why, and what to do next.


Zoom also announced ZRA Elite, a new tier that combines Zoom Revenue Accelerator Premium with Engage and Forecast in one offering.


[Liz Miller](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lizkmiller/) , VP and Principal Analyst at Constellation Research, described the broader opportunity: "Zoom is in an intensely unique position to deliver a far more unified and cohesive message around how the data, insights, and knowledge derived from all points of the ecosystem tie into the totality of the Salesforce vision."

## What use cases does Zoom's unified revenue operating system support?


- **Inbound-to-pipeline signal routing:** A prospective customer contacts your support team before converting.[Zoom Virtual Agent](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/virtual-agent/) handles the initial interaction while Zoom AI Companion surfaces conversation context to the account team, helping to close the gap between the service experience and the sales handoff.
- **Churn signal detection:** Common Room by Zoom tracks product engagement and community activity to surface accounts showing early signs of reduced activity.
- **[Post-call coaching at scale](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/cx-in-action-prevent-agent-burnout/) :** Customer conversations in Zoom Contact Center generates coaching data. Workforce Management and Quality Management tools use that data to identify the behaviors that drive resolution and build training programs around them.
- **Signal-driven outreach prioritization:** Rather than sequencing outreach based on a static prospect list, Engage uses buyer signals from Common Room to prioritize follow-up based on actual in-market behavior, which is designed to help reduce wasted outreach cycles and improve rep time-to-value.
- **Conversation-grounded forecasting:** Forecast uses conversation intelligence from Zoom Revenue Accelerator to assess deal health based on what was actually said in calls, not just what was entered in a CRM field, and is designed to ground[pipeline confidence scores](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/conversation-intelligence/features/revenue-intelligence/) in conversation data in addition to CRM fields, giving revenue leaders a more complete view of deal health.


These use cases are most valuable to teams that have connected their CX and revenue operations on a shared platform rather than managing them in separate systems.


## How does Zoom approach connected CX and revenue?


The thread running through every session, product announcement, and use case at Dreamforce 2026 was the same: visibility is the advantage.


On the CX side, Kentis showed that deploying AI is only the first step. The real value comes from running the full loop — connecting journeys, generating insights, routing actions, measuring outcomes, and feeding what you learn back into the system. On the revenue side, Dina showed what happens when that same discipline meets buyer intelligence: signals become outreach, conversations become coaching and deal data, and each closed or lost deal sharpens the next forecast.


Neither loop works in isolation. CX signals without revenue execution leave pipeline on the table. Revenue tools without reliable CX data are optimizing on incomplete information. The case Zoom made at Dreamforce is that connecting both on a single platform — where customer interactions, buyer intelligence, and sales execution share a data layer is how teams can move from reactive to compounding.


For CX leaders, the next step is closing the feedback loop on AI deployments already in motion. For revenue leaders, it's connecting buyer signals to the conversations and deals that actually move pipeline. For both, it starts with[visibility](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/connected-customer-experiences/) .

## Zoom Dreamforce 2026 FAQs


**Q1: What is an intelligent revenue system?**


An intelligent revenue operating system is a connected platform that integrates buyer intelligence, customer conversations, sales engagement, and pipeline forecasting in a single workflow. An intelligent revenue operating system surfaces signals and routes those signals into actions that can help advance a deal, retain an account, or help improve pipeline visibility.


Revenue teams use the concept to help reduce the gap between what sales and customer teams know and what teams can act on before a buying signal, churn indicator, or pipeline risk becomes harder to address.


**Q2: How does Zoom's unified revenue operating system work for sales teams?**


Zoom's unified intelligent revenue operating system connects three components in a unified sales workflow. Common Room by Zoom surfaces buyer signals and helps identify in-market accounts. Engage sequences and prioritizes multichannel outreach based on those signals. Zoom Revenue Accelerator Forecast uses conversation intelligence and deal-level data to help improve pipeline visibility and update CRM systems with suggested information.


ZRA Elite combines Zoom Revenue Accelerator Premium with Engage and Forecast in a single offering for revenue teams.


**Q3: What do best practices for AI contact center deployment look like?**


AI contact center deployment best practices begin with defining the desired outcome before selecting the technology. Effective deployments include connected customer journeys, AI models tuned to actual customer intents, measurement frameworks based on resolution and other meaningful outcomes, and feedback loops that allow the system to improve over time.


The framework presented at Dreamforce includes connected journeys, AI-generated insights, action routing, outcome measurement, and closed-loop learning. Organizations that deploy AI without a mechanism for measuring performance and improving future interactions are more likely to find that the investment is live but not yet delivering expected results.


For a deeper look at the framework, see[How to turn your CX AI ambitions into reality](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/how-to-turn-your-cx-ai-ambitions-into-reality/) .


**Q4: What does the five-stage AI deployment loop look like in practice?**


The five-stage loop starts with connected journeys — ensuring context follows the customer across channels and handoffs. From there, CX Insights generates data-driven patterns from interactions. AI Expert Assist routes those insights into real-time agent guidance. Quality Management measures outcomes across all captured interactions, not just a sample. And Workforce Management closes the loop by feeding performance data back into coaching, training, and scheduling.


In practice, a team running the full loop might discover through CX Insights that a specific inquiry type has a declining resolution rate, use Quality Management to pinpoint the root cause, deploy targeted coaching through Workforce Management, and then measure whether the next cycle of interactions improves.


**Q5: What is Common Room by Zoom?**


Common Room by Zoom is a buyer intelligence platform that aggregates signals from product activity, digital engagement, and community interactions to help identify in-market accounts, expansion opportunities, and churn risk.


Zoom acquired Common Room in July 2026 and made Common Room available through the Zoom platform at Dreamforce 2026. Common Room provides the intelligence layer that informs Engage's outreach sequencing and Forecast's pipeline modeling.


**Q6: What is the ZRA Elite tier announced at Dreamforce 2026?**


ZRA Elite is a Zoom Revenue Accelerator tier that combines Premium, Engage, and Forecast in a single offering for revenue teams. The tier is designed for B2B teams that want conversation intelligence, multichannel sales sequencing, and AI-powered pipeline forecasting under one subscription.


Zoom Revenue Accelerator is available in three tiers: Essentials, Premium, and Elite. Revenue leaders can evaluate ZRA Elite against an existing combination of conversation intelligence, sales engagement, and forecasting tools.


**Q7: How do CX and sales teams benefit from a shared platform?**


When CX and sales teams operate on a shared platform, customer signals generated during post-sale interactions can become available to revenue teams, while revenue insights can help inform customer-facing workflows.


For example, a customer who contacts support about a product limitation may be generating a churn signal that the account team can address before renewal. A shared platform connects that signal to revenue workflows without relying solely on manual escalation.


The practical implication is a go-to-market model in which the contact center contributes to revenue intelligence rather than operating only as a cost center. Zoom connects Zoom Contact Center conversations and operational data with Zoom Revenue Accelerator sales execution tools so organizations can use customer interactions to help improve retention and revenue growth.


For teams ready to act on customer and revenue signals, see[Running your business with CX data](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/running-your-business-with-cx-data/) .
